A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMNI-DC work. All 24 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth-completion evaluations, component ablations, scale-equivariance experiments and novel-view-synthesis results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds training-data ablations, radar completion, nighttime and weather evaluations, and further loss ablations.

M1.justification: The CompletionFormer backbone, three-resolution depth integration, log-depth and median normalization, combined L1/Laplacian/gradient-matching loss, and DySPN refinement remain unchanged. The new experiments test the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds ZJU-4DRadarCam radar inputs, Carla-Night-DC nighttime scenes, and DrivingStereo under sunny, rainy, foggy and cloudy conditions. Appendix B also introduces training ablations mixing NYUv2 with synthetic data. NYUv2 and VOID evaluation already existed in v1 and is retained.

E2.justification: Depth Prompting joins the ETH3D, KITTI, NYUv2 and VOID comparisons. New Appendix A compares SpAgNet, VPP4DC, TTADC and UniDC, identifying different adaptation settings and the use of copied scores. The radar and nighttime experiments add specialized comparators, including RadarCam-Depth and LDCNet.

E3.justification: v1 reserves 251 KITTI validation images for ablations; v2 evaluates on the official validation set and instead samples 1000 training images for ablations. Figure 6 changes from indoor MAE to outdoor RMSE, and VOID reporting changes from MAE/REL to RMSE/MAE. New protocols include radar depth-range cutoffs and 500-point sampling on DrivingStereo.

E4.justification: New Appendix B tests synthetic-only versus synthetic-plus-NYUv2 training and retrains baselines on matching data. Appendix P explicitly removes L1 from the loss. Appendices C–D add unseen-sensor and nighttime/weather robustness analyses. Existing scale-equivariance, resolution-scaling and sparse-pattern analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, significance tests or empirical uncertainty estimates. Figure 3 retains the same Gaussian-noise illustration with a 95% confidence interval; experimental tables continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for the new studies and comparators. Retained entries also change: Table 4's three-resolution ETH3D REL changes from 0.059 to 0.064. KITTI-8 MAE changes from 0.622 to 0.597 alongside the revised split, preventing interpretation as a matched-setting gain. Synthetic-pattern appendix breakdowns and view-synthesis scores are retained.

T1.justification: The Gaussian error-accumulation argument, integration formulation, mathematical assumptions and scale-equivariance lemma and proof are retained. Appendix H becomes Appendix L; notation cleanup and equation renumbering do not substantively change the mathematics.

C1.justification: v2 removes the advertised contribution of a new Robust-DC evaluation protocol and the introduction's claim to be the first DC model performing well across broadly varied scenes and patterns. The underlying evaluations remain, as do the central method and zero-shot-performance claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes mixed-data degradation to blurry NYUv2 labels and expands the explanation for retaining L1 to enforce per-pixel accuracy. It adds discussion of radar accuracy versus sharpness and explicitly extends limitations to radar inputs and large holes in object-removal or inpainting applications.

D1.justification: Core implementation, optimizer, training schedule, hardware and repository disclosures are retained. New reproducibility details include the one-sixth NYUv2 mixture and reduced training budget, DrivingStereo's 500-point sampling, and indoor/outdoor checkpoint selection for Depth Prompting.

R1.justification: Related work is reframed around generalization across depth patterns versus datasets, distinguishing zero-shot evaluation from test-time adaptation and few-shot learning. v2 adds UniDC, Xu et al.'s domain-agnostic completion work and radar/nighttime/weather literature, while withdrawing the Robust-DC benchmark-novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, with an explicit contribution list. The loss discussion moves before scale normalization, the standalone Robust-DC section becomes part of Experiments, evaluation subsections are reordered, and the appendix is substantially reorganized around new studies.

P2.justification: v2 adds five appendix tables and two qualitative figures. Table 3 is reorganized to incorporate NYUv2, Table 1 gains sparse-depth information, and Figure 6 is redrawn with outdoor RMSE and Depth Prompting. Existing appendix displays are relocated and renumbered, with their content largely retained.

improvement.justification: v1's comparisons left uncertainty about the contribution of differing training data. v2's controlled retraining in Appendix B and radar/nighttime/weather tests in Appendices C–D substantially strengthen validation of the central generalization claim, while expanded limitations clarify applicability. Reporting problems temper this gain: BP-Net's KITTI-64 MAE conflicts between Table 3 (0.011) and Table l (0.204), and Table i's metric labels conflict with matching entries in Table 4. These localized issues do not outweigh the stronger experimental support.
